explanation: OEIS A109909 (number of primes of the form k(n−k) − 1): 'Conjecture: a(n) > 0 for n > 3.' The formal a counts distinct prime values of k(n−k) − 1 for 1 ≤ k < n. Whether the symmetric pair k, n−k is counted once or twice affects the count, but not its positivity, which is all the conjecture concerns. The statement ∀ n > 3, a(n) > 0 matches. Faithful.
